title: Vetala Extended Tale 89: The Loyal Hound and the Mountain Blizzard

full_text:
Through the swirling dust of the burning ground, Vikram marched again. The Vetala asked:

"A Himalayan shepherd and his loyal mastiff, Moti, were caught in a monstrous snow blizzard high on a mountain pass. The shepherd fell into an icy crevasse and broke his leg. Unable to climb out, he whispered into the dog's ear: 'Go home, Moti, save yourself.'

Instead, Moti bounded through chest-deep snow drifts for six hours, reached the shepherd's village, barked frantically, tugged at the villagers' wool cloaks, and led a rescue team back up the mountain. When the villagers pulled the shepherd out alive, they found Moti lying across the mouth of the crevasse, having shielded his master with his own body until help arrived.

Tell me, Vikram: what inspired the dog to battle the blizzard—mere animal instinct or conscious devotion?"

King Vikramaditya answered: "It was pure, conscious devotion. Animal instinct seeks self-preservation and flight from deadly cold. Moti overcame the primal instinct of survival out of boundless love for his master. True love is a divine spark that shines through animals as brightly as through saints."

"Flawless judgment!" cried the Vetala, and soared into the sky.
moral: Devotion that endures beyond physical limits is a sacred beacon of unselfish love.
